info.bio:
Bill Haley ( Highland Park,Detroit,Estados Unidos,6 de julio de 1925 - Texas, Estados Unidos, 9 de febrero de 1981)
 Su nombre completo era William John Clifton Haley (pronunciado IPA:[ˈheɪliː], aprox. hey-lii) fue un músico estadounidense, uno de los fundadores del rock and roll, nacido en Highland Park, un barrio de Detroit.

 Estilo y Origen del Rock 'n' Roll 

Hay quienes datan el origen del rock and roll en 1954, con el trabajo discográfico de Bill Haley y su grupo "Bill Haley and his Comets"

scenes.name: Rock'n'roll
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Fusión de rhythm'n'blues y country, con mucho más peso del primero. Chuck Berry inventa en 1955 el rock'n'roll tal como se conocerá durante cincuenta años (la guitarra como instrumento protagonista, canciones propias que hablan a los adolescentes); Bo Diddley aporta el ritmo «hambone», Little Richard y Esquerita el histerismo y el maquillaje (el primer «decadence-rock»), Jerry Lee Lewis el piano feroz y Sun Records el rockabilly. Elvis Presley es, para Scaruffi, «la primera gran estafa del rock'n'roll». Buddy Holly y Eddie Cochran abren otra vía; en paralelo nacen el soul (Ray Charles), la exótica (Martin Denny, Esquivel), la música electrónica de cinta y, en Gran Bretaña, el skiffle.

podcast.title: Explosion into Public Consciousness (1955)
podcast.body: Bill Haley, along with Elvis, Chuck Berry, Little Richard, and Bo Diddly, exploded into public consciousness in 1955, marking the birth of rock and roll. "they all exploded into public consciousness that year, 1955, the birth of rock and roll."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: End of First Wave Rockabilly Success (1956)
podcast.body: By December 1956, Bill Haley had stopped having hit records, indicating the close of the first wave of rockabilly stars, leaving Elvis Presley as the sole white rock and roll star from that initial period. "Karl Perkins, Gene Vincent and Bill Haley had stopped having hits, and Johnny Cash had started to be promoted as a country singer, rather than a rock and roller."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Unique Status in Early Rock and Roll (1956)
podcast.body: In 1956, Bill Haley was one of only two rock and roll artists (the other being Elvis Presley) who were in a "league of their own," meaning record labels understood how to market and build their audiences, unlike the struggles faced with other rock and roll acts. "They were Bill Haley and Elvis, who were in a league of their own."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 40: "Drugstore Rock 'n' Roll" by Janis Martin

podcast.title: Film Repurposing - "Don't Knock the Rock"
podcast.body: Bill Haley's second film was "Don't Knock the Rock," also produced by Sam Kertzmann. This film's title was echoed when Kertzmann produced Chubby Checker's second twist film, "Don't Knock the Twist." "As Kertzmann had also made Bill Haley's second film, Don't Knock the Rock, so Checker's second film became Don't Knock the Twist."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Film Repurposing - "Rock Around the Clock"
podcast.body: Sam Kertzmann, the producer of "Twist Around the Clock" starring Chubby Checker, had previously produced "Rock Around the Clock," a film starring Bill Haley in the 1950s. Kertzmann easily repurposed the script from Haley's film for Checker's twist film. "Twist around the clock was an easy film to make because Sam Kertzmann, who produced it, had produced several rock films in the 50s, including Rock Around the Clock."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Inspired by Louis Jordan
podcast.body: Bill Haley was one of the artists who drew inspiration from Louis Jordan, who led the most popular R&B group in the late 1940s and early 1950s. "The one that inspired everyone from Chuck Berry to Bill Haley."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Limited Imitation
podcast.body: Despite his prominence, his specific musical style had few imitators within American rock and roll. However, early British rock and roll groups, such as Tony Cromby and the Rocket, often produced "anemic copies" of his less successful records. "As we discussed in the episodes on Haley, his particular style of music had few imitators in American rock and roll, so while British groups were copying things like Fettie Bell's one-hit, Gideoparding Dong."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 70: "Move It" by Cliff Richard and the Drifters

podcast.title: Rockabilly Fizzle
podcast.body: Bill Haley was one of the white rockabilly artists who gained prominence in 1955 and 1956, but whose momentum on the US charts declined significantly by late 1956, preventing him from securing another major domestic hit. He, like other rockabilly acts, found continued success and produced important music internationally. "While Perkins, Gene Vincent and Bill Haley would between them never have another major hit in the US, though all of them would have success in other countries and make important music over the next few years."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Twist Record (Year?)
podcast.body: Bill Haley recorded a twist record during the widespread craze, though many such cash-in records were deemed "terrible." "There were twist records by Bill Haley, Neil Sedarka, Dwayne Eddie, almost all of these were terrible records."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
